books.section: Prosperity and a New World Order (1988–2000)

stem: In which year shown was unemployment highest?

options.misconception: Unemployment in 2000 was 4.0 percent, the lowest figure in the table.
Unemployment in 1990 was 5.6 percent, well below the highest figure.
Unemployment in 2008 was 5.8 percent, well below the highest figure.

rationales.A: Unemployment in 2000 was 4.0 percent, the lowest figure in the table.
rationales.B: Unemployment in 1990 was 5.6 percent, well below the highest figure.
rationales.C: Unemployment in 2008 was 5.8 percent, well below the highest figure.
rationales.D: The table shows 9.7 percent in 1982, higher than 9.6 percent in 2010 and every other year shown.
rationales.general:
1. Scan the column for the biggest number: 9.7 percent.
2. Check its year: 1982.
3. Watch the near miss: 2010 reached 9.6 percent, just one tenth of a point lower, so read both numbers.
4. The lowest year, 2000, sits at the other end at 4.0 percent.
Remember: in a table, the biggest number wins — but check the close second.

stimulus.source_note: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Population Survey, annual averages (series LNU04000000).
stimulus.text:
| Year | Unemployment rate |
| 1980 | 7.2% |
| 1982 | 9.7% |
| 1990 | 5.6% |
| 2000 | 4.0% |
| 2008 | 5.8% |
| 2009 | 9.3% |
| 2010 | 9.6% |

Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Population Survey (annual averages). Simplified for this test.
